column1: # DISCLOSURE_CHECKS.tsv — every published "this is not checkable / no public artifact" disclosure,
# paired with the command that PROVES it is still true.
# 🔴 THE GATE FIRES WHEN THE PROOF COMMAND SUCCEEDS. That is deliberate and is the whole point: a
# disclosure saying "no public artifact exists" becomes FALSE the moment the artifact ships, and
# nothing was watching for that. TR-6 carried such a disclosure (the wording is registered as
# RP-2805ae9c; it is NOT quoted here, because quoting a retracted string in a tracked file is how
# it survives a retraction) for three days after `fcd9feab` (2026-09-03) put the DRAT certificates
# on `main` — and
# MIAH_PROSPECTIVE_AUDIT_2026_09_05.md then cited those very lines as EXEMPLARY house style, two
# days after they became false. Found 2026-09-06 by a Codex lens-B pass, adjudicated by Fable.
# Understating what you can prove is a defect of the same family as overstating it: both make the
# published text disagree with the repository.
# file<TAB>claim-substring<TAB>artifact-exists-test (shell; exit 0 == THE ARTIFACT EXISTS == disclosure is STALE)
# TR-6's row was REMOVED 2026-09-06 after the disclosure was corrected. It moved to
# documentation/RETRACTED_PHRASES.tsv, which is the right home once a claim is retracted rather than
# merely stale: that registry already has the allowlist mechanism for a correction note that QUOTES
# the retracted wording, which this gate does not and should not grow a second copy of. This gate
# watches LIVE disclosures; that one watches retracted ones. Keeping the row here made the gate fire
# on the correction's own quotation of the phrase it retracts -- the "gate correct data fails" class,
# for the third time in one night.
# Q-955 (2026-10-03; Codex Q835 push-path review P-08, A02#19): the two rows below carried the
# probe `false` from the day they were added (0465889e), so they could never fire, and the gate
# read every nonzero probe rc as "still true". The gate now takes a THREE-VALUED probe (0 = the
# artifact exists, 1 = the disclosure still holds, anything else = the probe could not answer,
# which is a FAIL) and refuses a constant probe. Each row now probes its own subject:
#  - TR-11 (the 24/25/27/28-pair Spot validation ladder, "no public artifact backs these four
#    integers"): the retained records are session logs and manifests, so the artifact exists when
#    a tracked file that is not prose or source (.md, .py, .c, .h, .sh) carries one of the four
#    integers, with or without thousands commas. Source is excluded on purpose: verify.py and
#    reports/evidence/f1/f3_rung_b0_cleanroom.py hold them as EXPECTED values, not as run records.
#    `git grep` answers 0/1, and 128 outside a repository.
#  - TR-12 (the single-branch-exhaustion shortfall factor, "no public reproduction command"): its
#    reproduction command is the XA-c/d query, which yields a factor only once a node-mapping
#    certificate exists. The published verdict record reports/tr12/VERDICTS.txt says which: the
#    artifact exists when TR12_XA_CD reads PASS or ONE-SIDED:<kind> rather than PENDING/SKIP. A
#    missing file, or anything but exactly one TR12_XA_CD line, is rc 2.
